JIMMY & WAX CROSS PROJECT CONNECTIVITY AND READINESS AUDIT
25 October 2026 | Dashboard, website, backend and Flutter customer app

VERDICT

The core is connected and passes substantial local verification. The system is
not yet fully connected across every customer feature, and production readiness
is not established. The largest gaps are multi-variant catalogue handling,
website catalogue media/navigation, mobile order history/tracking, customer
self-service, real providers and repeatable release configuration.

No meaningful single completion percentage can be derived from the tests: a
passing endpoint or screen does not prove every write, provider or device flow.

SCOPE AND METHOD

Audited these exact local projects:
  Dashboard: C:/Users/MSI/OneDrive/Desktop/jimmy&wax_dashboard
  Website:   C:/Users/MSI/OneDrive/Desktop/jimmy_nd _wax_website
  Backend:   C:/Users/MSI/OneDrive/Desktop/jimmy&wax_backend
  App:       C:/Users/MSI/OneDrive/Desktop/jimmy&wax_app

The running architecture is a Next.js operator dashboard with a server-side API
proxy, a React/Vite website, a Flutter app, an Express commerce API, a separate
read-only experience API, PostgreSQL, and background workers. One gateway routes
public reads to the experience API and commerce/admin requests to the commerce
API. Redis is optional shared rate-limit storage. The active app uses the
Express API; the Supabase dependency and older migration/docs remain in its tree.

Local verification used a separate PostgreSQL container on port 55432 and two
new databases: jimmywax_audit_test and jimmywax_audit_live. Business mutations,
test accounts, orders, publications and rollback occurred only there. Existing
business databases and source implementation were not changed. Existing seven
dashboard contract modifications were preserved.

No real deployed domain was identified from the supplied project configuration;
the origins found are local addresses and deployment placeholders. These results
therefore certify the stated local checks, not a production deployment. Real
Razorpay/Shiprocket transactions, email/SMS delivery and native device release
tests were not performed. Available Razorpay configuration was not used to spend
money or contact the provider.

  Dashboard contract lock:                 PASS, v1.5.0
  Dashboard TypeScript, lint and build:     PASS

  Authenticated dashboard browser sweep:   PASS, 38 routes, no HTTP 5xx or JS exceptions
  Dashboard sign-in and MFA enrollment:    PASS in browser
  Dashboard cookie properties:             Secure, SameSite=Strict; session HttpOnly
  Studio save/publish/website/rollback:    PASS against real local services
  Backend OpenAPI vs implemented routes:   PASS, 238 documented / 238 served operations
  Backend unit tests:                      PASS, 9 files / 73 tests
  Backend database integration tests:      PASS, 17 files / 206 tests
  Backend direct TypeScript checks:        PASS, all 11 app/package tsconfigs
  Backend package typecheck script:        INEFFECTIVE here; see finding 12
  Website unit tests:                      PASS, 2 files / 68 tests
  Website production build:                PASS, with chunk/sitemap warnings
  Website existing browser tests:          PASS, 8 tests using mocked API fixtures
  Website real COD customer journey:       PASS against real local services
  Flutter analysis/tests/native build:     NOT RUN; configured SDK is missing

The real COD journey verified guest cart, demo OTP authentication, cart merge,
address/serviceability, authoritative quote, order creation, admin visibility,
and session/order persistence after browser reload. Demo OTP verifies the
integration mechanics; it does not demonstrate real SMS delivery.

The Studio journey saved through the dashboard's authenticated server proxy,
validated and published a web release, observed the changed text on the actual
website, then rolled back and observed the original text return.

An additional source-reference heuristic found all 164 documented admin
operations referenced under dashboard src/. This is useful coverage inventory,
not proof that all 164 operations were exercised successfully.

PRIORITIZED FINDINGS AND REQUIRED WORK

1. HIGH -- Update dependencies before public release

   Registry audits report dashboard: 2 critical and 2 high advisories; backend
   workspace: 2 critical, 3 high and 3 moderate; website: 2 high dependency entries.
   Counts are advisory/dependency scan results, not demonstrated exploit counts.
   The backend workspace Next.js findings belong to its retired apps/admin
   package; the active commerce and experience services run Express.

   Next.js 16.3.8 falls within reported affected ranges. The two critical findings
   are conditional: the image advisory's documented sharp workaround is already
   satisfied by dashboard sharp 0.35.5, and no dashboard use-cache function or
   cacheComponents setting was found. The Dockerfile also uses Alpine. Do not
   describe this audit as proving an exploitable dashboard RCE. Upgrade Next.js
   to the maintained patched release (advisories identify 16.4.1), align
   eslint-config-next, and rerun tests.

   The active commerce service resolves body-parser 2.3.0 and uses Express JSON,
   raw and URL-encoded parsers with default decompression. Its high-severity
   compressed-body process-crash advisory is relevant to these public parsers.
   Update the Express dependency graph to body-parser 2.4.0 or newer, or apply
   the maintainer's documented mitigation after compatibility review.

   Update Zod past 4.6.5 (patched minimum 4.6.6), backend Nodemailer (advisories
   identify 10.1.4), and the website Vite/source-map-js dependency graph. Vite is
   currently a production dependency, but its dev-server issues should not be
   equated with vulnerability of a static-only deployed dist/ site.

   Evidence: package.json, backend/package.json, backend/apps/admin/package.json,
   website/package.json, and the three dependency JSON files in the evidence folder.
   Advisory sources:
   https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw
   https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr
   https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5
   https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828

2. HIGH -- Multi-variant products duplicate and disappear across pages

   Reproduced with a second synthetic active variant for an existing product.
   A full public catalogue page returned both rows with the same product ID.
   Walking limit=1 pages returned only one variant for that product: the other
   was skipped. The database view produces one row per active variant, while
   the cursor only includes (sort_order, product_id). Product detail also selects
   the first row without an explicit variant choice. Clients key products by
   product ID and have no complete variant-selection flow.

   Fix the public contract deliberately: return a product with its variants and
   let the client select one, or use unique variant keys/cursors consistently.
   Test two or more active variants, same-product page boundaries, PDP selection,
   price/stock changes and checkout with each variant on both clients.

   Evidence: backend/apps/experience-api/src/app.ts:250-278;
   db/migrations/20261004100000_b9_experience_studio.sql:15;
   variant-pagination.json in the evidence folder.

3. HIGH -- Dashboard product images do not drive the native website catalogue

   Website ApiProduct does not consume the backend media array. toProduct()
   picks pictures and films from the hard-coded PRESENTATION map; unknown
   products get a generic collection image. A dashboard product image change
   therefore does not update the native shop/PDP/cart presentation.

   Use approved backend product media as the primary gallery, retaining bundled
   presentation as an explicit fallback. Verify upload -> approval -> product
   assignment -> website listing/PDP/cart without changing website code.

   Evidence: website/src/data/products.ts:85-104.
   Studio page-block media is a separate path and is implemented; this finding
   concerns native catalogue presentation.

4. HIGH -- Website category and collection actions lose their destination

   resolveAction() maps every category and collection to /shop, dropping the ID
   or slug. Profile/addresses actions map to orders; help maps to the brand story.
   These links resolve safely but do not implement their requested destination.

   Add category/collection routes or URL filters backed by the corresponding
   API. Give profile, address management and support their actual destinations.
   Test a Studio CTA through to the intended filtered products or account screen.

   Evidence: website/src/lib/actions.ts:29-46.

5. HIGH -- Mobile order history and tracking are only partially connected

   loadUserData() requests orders with limit=1. The app stores latestOrder rather
   than a history collection. OrdersScreen displays one order and hard-codes
   'Order placed'. TrackingScreen constructs OrderDetailView without passing
   live status, so it defaults to placed. There is no repository shipment-fetch
   path connecting dashboard fulfilment changes to this timeline.

   Build paginated order history, server status/payment fields and shipment/event
   loading with refresh. Verify dashboard processing -> shipped -> delivered and
   cancellation/payment expiry in the customer's app, including older orders.

   Evidence: app/lib/core/data/api_store_repository.dart:203-241;
   app/lib/main.dart:3705-3800; app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_view.dart:27.

6. HIGH -- Mobile historical receipts depend on the current catalogue

   _orderFromJson() reconstructs order items by looking up current products and
   drops lines whose products no longer exist in that catalogue. It discards the
   historical name/variant/unit-price data already supplied by order lines.
   OrdersScreen then accesses purchase.items.first without an empty-list guard.
   Archiving all products in an old order can produce an empty receipt and an
   unsafe access; changing a current product can also change its old receipt.

   Introduce an immutable order-line model from the order response, keep images
   optional, and safely render archived/deleted products and missing media.
   This is a code-traced failure path; native runtime reproduction is outstanding.

   Evidence: app/lib/core/data/api_store_repository.dart:361-383;
   app/lib/core/data/catalog.dart:65; app/lib/main.dart:3725.

7. HIGH -- Real customer SMS sign-in needs implementation

   SMS_PROVIDER supports only none or console. ConsoleSmsSender logs messages;
   the production main service never uses it for real delivery. The demo phone
   path works locally, but other phone numbers cannot receive production OTPs
   through the current implementation. Supplying a vendor key alone is insufficient.

   Implement a real provider adapter, configure the approved sender/template,
   and verify delivery, cooldown, expiry, abuse limits and provider failures.
   Evidence: backend/packages/config/src/index.ts:46-48;
   backend/packages/integrations/src/sms.ts; backend/apps/commerce-api/src/main.ts.

8. HIGH -- Customer self-service is behind backend/admin capability

   The backend has returns, invoice, reviews, notification and account endpoints.
   The website has no complete customer return/refund request, invoice access,
   wishlist/review submission, notification inbox, or account export/deletion UI.
   The app supports wishlist, reviews and preference saving, but does not connect
   customer returns, invoices, cancellation, account export/deletion or a real
   notification inbox through its current repository/screen flows.

   Add these journeys in a declared launch scope rather than counting the
   existence of backend routes as finished customer features. A phone-only account
   also needs OTP reauthentication for deletion: the backend deletion endpoint
   currently demands a password and deleteAccount() verifies password_hash,
   while phone-created accounts can have no password.

   Evidence: backend/apps/commerce-api/src/serviceRoutes.ts;
   backend/apps/commerce-api/src/authRoutes.ts:370;
   backend/packages/commerce-domain/src/identity.ts:431-435;
   website/src/lib/shop.ts; app/lib/core/data/api_store_repository.dart.

9. HIGH -- Policies are not connected to the customer experience

   The app's policy destinations still open SetupRequiredPolicyScreen even
   though the backend offers published content endpoints. Website checkout has
   a terms statement without a connected terms destination in that flow.

   Supply official store copy and route privacy/terms/shipping/returns pages to
   the same published backend content on both clients. Verify navigation from
   checkout, account and footer and document the policy version displayed.
   Evidence: app/lib/main.dart:4458; website/src/pages/Checkout.tsx;
   backend/apps/experience-api/src/app.ts:337-360.

10. HIGH -- Real fulfilment, refunds and outbound messages need provider acceptance

   Manual fulfilment and fake-provider shipping/payment logic have integration
   coverage. This audit did not verify real Razorpay capture/refund, webhook
   delivery, Shiprocket dispatch/labels/pickup, real SMTP delivery or bounce handling.
   Local credential presence does not establish that these flows work externally.
   Shiprocket createReturn() explicitly throws 'Reverse pickups are not implemented'.

   Complete a controlled provider acceptance sequence and reconcile the result
   against dashboard and customer views. Implement reverse pickup or explicitly
   provide a manual operational path before promising automated returns.
   Evidence: backend/packages/integrations/src/shipping.ts:736-744;
   backend/apps/workers/src/main.ts; backend/packages/commerce-domain/src/payments.ts.

11. HIGH -- Contract versions have drifted between projects

   Canonical backend OpenAPI and dashboard copy: v1.5.0, identical SHA-256
   eee7a28b09bdd20a2f98a07d3f28e3bdc18d7ad46ae12ebbd02978166ca63d3c.
   Backend contracts/pack/openapi.yaml: v1.4.0-draft.1.
   App contracts/api/openapi.yaml: v0.1.0-draft.
   Website uses handwritten types with no pinned shared contract gate.

   Refresh the generated pack and app contract from the canonical source, pin
   consumption by hash/version, and check all clients in CI. The stale app file
   does not prove that all its runtime requests are stale: current repository
   code already calls modern endpoints. Documentation and automated guarantees
   are what demonstrably disagree.

12. HIGH -- Backend typecheck can succeed without checking any project

   pnpm typecheck printed 'No projects matched the filters' and exited 0 in the
   installed Windows/pnpm environment. Direct tsc runs against all 11 tsconfigs
   passed, so this is a verification-gate defect rather than a discovered type error.

   Make workspace selection reliable and fail if zero projects match. Record
   the number of checked packages and prove the gate rejects a deliberate type
   error in a temporary test branch. CI on Linux was not run here.
   Evidence: backend/package.json:10; backend-direct-types.log.

13. HIGH -- Production Compose needs service-specific configuration

   Commerce, experience and workers inherit the same .env.prod, including one
   DATABASE_URL and provider/signing secrets. The example DATABASE_URL is the
   commerce login despite the runbook requiring separate login roles per service.
   Experience/workers do not override TRUST_PROXY_HOPS, while loadConfig() applies
   its production proxy requirement to every service. The supplied templates
   therefore need completion and service-specific overrides before deployment.

   Provide separate database URLs and minimal secrets per service, validate each
   actual environment, and smoke-test the built topology with migrations, workers,
   gateway/CORS, storage and readiness checks. Permission tests with deliberately
   separate roles do not prove that this shared-env deployment preserves them.
   Evidence: infrastructure/prod/docker-compose.prod.yml:7-34;
   infrastructure/prod/.env.prod.example; backend/packages/config/src/index.ts;
   docs/build/PRODUCTION_RUNBOOK.md:25-26.

14. HIGH -- Source control and reproducibility are incomplete

   The backend Git repository has no commits and no tracked files; the whole
   backend, contracts, migrations, infrastructure and .data are untracked.
   Website and app paths are not inside Git repositories. The dashboard does
   have Git history and existing uncommitted contract changes.

   Establish version control/backups for the three projects, exclude credentials,
   storage/runtime data and generated artifacts, then commit reviewed source,
   migrations, lockfiles and deployment configuration. Add CI for website/app and
   a release manifest tying all four revisions to the same contract version.
   Do not blindly git-add the backend root: .data and runtime content are present.

15. RELEASE BLOCKER -- Mobile tooling and signing still need a verified release

   flutter is unavailable on PATH and the configured SDK at
   C:/Users/MSI/Downloads/flutter no longer exists. Fresh Flutter analysis/tests
   could not run. Existing screenshots, APKs and prior test logs are historical
   evidence only. Android still uses com.example.jimmy_wax_app; release signing
   intentionally requires owner keys. iOS signing/archive needs macOS.

   Restore/configure the SDK, run the complete app test suite, verify the live API
   adapter on a device, approve permanent app IDs/domains, configure private
   signing, and test signed releases including hosted payment return and links.
   Evidence: app/android/local.properties; app/.dart_tool/package_config.json;
   app/android/app/build.gradle.kts; app/docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md.

16. MEDIUM -- Website catalogue and history stop at the first page

   Catalogue reads limit=50 and ignores nextCursor; orders does the same.
   Sitemap generation fetches one product page with limit=100. Larger catalogues
   and customer histories silently lose entries; PDP lookup also depends on the
   loaded catalogue list. Implement pagination and direct detail fetching.
   Evidence: website/src/lib/catalog.tsx:42; website/src/lib/shop.ts:70;
   website/src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx; website/scripts/postbuild.mjs.

17. MEDIUM -- Improve website network and shipment error handling

   Website raw API fetch has no request deadline, so requests can leave forms
   waiting until the browser/network fails. shop.shipments() converts every
   failure to an empty list, making a tracking outage indistinguishable from
   no shipments. Add bounded reads, visible retry states and distinct empty/error
   states; preserve idempotency and never automatically replay unsafe writes.
   Evidence: website/src/lib/api.ts:73; website/src/lib/shop.ts:72.

18. MEDIUM -- Push and marketing delivery are not finished

   The backend stores device tokens and in-app notifications, but explicitly has
   no push delivery. Notification preferences and message templates do not make
   a customer push channel or marketing broadcast workflow. notify.ts states
   marketing is not implemented. Add a consent-aware sender and visible delivery
   state only if these channels are part of the intended launch scope.
   Evidence: backend/apps/commerce-api/src/serviceRoutes.ts:182;
   backend/packages/commerce-domain/src/notify.ts:30.

19. MEDIUM -- Release configuration and performance need stronger defaults

   The website production build currently succeeds with no SITE_ORIGIN and skips
   sitemap generation; its API origin falls back to localhost if no production
   value is supplied. The build warns about a 518.20 kB main JS chunk (159.70 kB
   gzip). Fail production preflight for missing/public-insecure origins and use
   route/component splitting where it improves the customer journey.

   Keep one approved package manager/lockfile per project instead of website
   npm and pnpm lockfiles plus latest dependency ranges. Split app/lib/main.dart
   (7,479 lines) into feature modules with clear state/repository boundaries.
   Remove retired dependencies/docs only after checking their remaining uses.

20. LOW -- Document the intentional dashboard media upload limit

   Dashboard video uploads stop at 15 MiB while the backend supports 100 MiB.
   The dashboard intentionally limits buffered request bodies and labels the UI
   accurately. This is an operational limit, not a silent connectivity failure.
   Add a streaming upload path and memory/load verification if larger campaigns
   are required. Evidence: src/lib/api/resources/media-validation.ts:3-11.

Real-provider and app-device checks remain explicit acceptance work; code
presence and fixture tests are not treated as live provider/device verification.

RECOMMENDED EXECUTION ORDER

1. Protect and stabilize the source: safe Git baselines/backups, dependency
   remediation, contract synchronization, reliable typecheck/CI, service-specific
   production configuration and restored Flutter tooling.
2. Fix catalogue propagation: variant contract/cursors and selection, backend
   product media on the website, category/collection destinations and pagination.
3. Finish post-purchase: immutable mobile receipts, full order history, real
   shipment status, cancellation, returns, invoices, policies and account controls.
4. Complete operational acceptance: real SMS and SMTP, Razorpay payment/refund
   callbacks, Shiprocket forward/reverse/manual workflows, signed Android/iOS
   builds, backups/restores, worker restarts and production monitoring.
5. Improve beyond launch: push/marketing if needed, route splitting, app feature
   extraction and larger media upload support.

ACCEPTANCE FOR A CONNECTED RELEASE

One reproducible staging run should create a product with two variants and
approved media in the dashboard, see/select both correctly on web and app, apply
a coupon, place COD and prepaid orders, see identical records in the dashboard,
ship them, see tracking on both clients, issue an invoice, submit/moderate a
review, request/decide a return and confirm the refund. Repeat after refresh,
network interruption, concurrent stock changes, worker restart and release
rollback. Run permission tests with non-admin roles and independent customers.
All four deployable revisions must identify the same canonical API version.

EVIDENCE

Saved under docs/build/evidence/cross-project-2026-10-25/:
  summary.json, live-browser.json, customer-browser.json, variant-pagination.json,
  dashboard-drift.log, dashboard-build.log, backend-direct-types.log,
  backend-integration.log, website-e2e.log, and dependency audit JSON reports.

The authenticated sweep contained an existing seeded-product validation alert
('The same image is listed twice') on the product editor; routes still loaded
without server errors. Clean that seeded media data before accepting a product
update. The sweep is not a claim that every form mutation or every viewport was
exercised. Accessibility/responsive and real device acceptance should be part
of the next release gate.
